scientific_question: Do the previously supported models remain useful across every contiguous interval of their respective datasets, and where do they fail?

fold_rule.construction: Sort unique x values and split them into five contiguous, nearly equal groups. Every repeated x value remains in exactly one group. Each group is tested once while the other four groups are used for fitting.
fold_rule.leakage_control: No observation shares an x value between a fold's fitting and test sets; every observation is evaluated exactly once
fold_rule.fit_rule: Use the existing frozen model equations, starts, bounds and optimizers. Fit only the other four groups; never select starts, parameters or models using the current test group
fold_rule.failure_rule: Optimizer failure, non-finite prediction or a test-group extrapolation failure is recorded as failure, not discarded or called success

baselines.linear: Ordinary least-squares linear response fitted on the other four groups
baselines.cubic_polynomial: Ordinary least-squares cubic polynomial fitted on the other four groups

metrics: Per-fold RMSE, MAE and maximum absolute residual
Every optimizer failure, non-finite value and fold where model RMSE exceeds baseline

interpretation_rule.robust_limited_support: All five folds produce finite predictions and every fold's model RMSE is no greater than its baseline RMSE
interpretation_rule.not_universally_supported: Any fold fails, produces non-finite predictions, or has model RMSE greater than baseline; report the exact fold rather than hiding it behind a median
interpretation_rule.scope: Five contiguous grouped folds per dataset are a stress diagnostic, not a universal model-family ranking or independent experimental replication

output_rule: Write validation/grouped-stress.json and papers/08_跨数据集压力测试/fig08_grouped_stress.png; preserve all folds and failures; refuse to overwrite existing results
